newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK capitalists to hail Beijing rule with huge gala. [CORRECTED 13:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: HK capitalists to hail Beijing rule with huge gala. [CORRECTED 13:00 GMT]

text.p: Hong Kong's business community unveiled plans on Tuesday for a multi-million dollar extravaganza (corrects to delete erroneous dollar figure) of fireworks, lasers, an illuminated barge flotilla and giant balloons to mark the first day of Chinese rule on July 1.
The festivities will signal an extraordinary welcome from a capitalist bastion to a communist state at an historic turning-point in the closing years of the 20th century.

A nonstop series of parties, ceremonies and public celebrations, billed as an Asian "party of the century", will mark the handover of Hong Kong, a British colony for 156 years, to China at midnight on June 30.

The fireworks show on July 1, organised by the Better Hong Kong Foundation, an affiliation of Hong Kong's billionaire businessmen, will also feature what the organisers bill as the world's largest outdoor karaoke show.
Leonie Ki, chief executive of the Better Hong Kong Foundation, said the organisers hoped the karaoke event would set a Guinness-recognised global record.

More than 30 big businesses have lined up to sponsor the event including key representatives of the British colonial establishment, the Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd and John Swire & Sons (Hong Kong) Ltd, whose names are synonomous with the colonialisation of Hong Kong.

Conspicuously absent is the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp Ltd, also regarded as a pillar of colonialism, although its subsidiary Hang Seng Bank Ltd featured on the list of companies which have donated HK$100 million (US$12.8 million) to fund the event (corrects donation sum from US$100 million).
Hongkong Bank spokesmen were not immediately available for comment.
The show will revolve around a central stage moored in Hong Kong's famous Victoria Harbour, creating a huge theatre in one of the world's best-known scenic panoramas.
The illuminated flotilla will comprise 31 decorated barges being constructed at shipyards in southern China. Eight barges will be dedicated to the fireworks display.

Hovering over this bustling port with its stunning backdrop of skyscrapers will be hot air balloons as high as 10-storey buildings. They will depict Hong Kong as the Pearl of the Orient, according to an artist's impression of the event.
An anthem has been commissioned for the occasion, called "Song of Peace", from Chinese composer Tan Dun. It will be performed by American-Chinese cellist Yo Yo Ma.
The show will be producecd by Don Mischer, who also mounted the opening and closing ceremonies for the Olympic Games in Atlanta last year.
